scientific_role: fresh split-sample empirical test of the temporal-buffering mechanism using the archived 55-species bird dataset

hypothesis.statement: Species with stronger historical temporal responsiveness of arrival date to green-up timing will show weaker holdout dependence of phase mismatch on the animal/environment speed ratio.
hypothesis.mechanistic_link: If seasonal timing buffers spatial tracking demand, greater timing responsiveness should flatten the holdout mismatch-versus-speed-ratio curve rather than generate one common speed optimum.

split_rule.order: ascending unique observed years after source-level availability only
split_rule.reason: chronological split prevents the holdout mismatch-speed relation from contributing to the temporal-responsiveness estimate

calibration_timing_gain.species_cell_arrival_baseline: mean(arr_GAM_mean) within species x cell over calibration years
calibration_timing_gain.cell_greenup_baseline: mean(gr_mn) across unique cell x year values within each cell over calibration years
calibration_timing_gain.standardized_timing_gain: z score of raw_timing_gain across eligible species, using calibration-only mean and SD

eligibility.observation_definition: finite arr_GAM_mean and gr_mn rows used in the calibration timing-gain model

holdout_phase_error.baseline_lag: mean(arr_GAM_mean - gr_mn) within species x cell over calibration years

primary_model.formula: abs_lag_deviation_holdout ~ log_speed_ratio + I(log_speed_ratio^2) + z_timing_gain + log_speed_ratio:z_timing_gain + I(log_speed_ratio^2):z_timing_gain + log_speed_scale + alignment + cell_lat2 + greenup_date_anom_from_calibration + mig_flag + breed_flag + s(species, bs='re') + s(species_cell, bs='re') + s(year_f, bs='re')

secondary_descriptive_outputs: primary coefficient estimate, SE, t statistic and p value
predicted holdout speed-ratio curves at z_timing_gain = -1, 0, +1
quadratic curvature implied at z_timing_gain = -1 and +1
holdout sample counts by year and species

claim_rule.PASS: Historical timing responsiveness weakens later movement-speed dependence, supporting temporal buffering as a natural moderator of spatial tracking demand.
claim_rule.FAIL_WRONG_DIRECTION: Historical timing responsiveness does not buffer later movement-speed dependence in the predicted direction.
claim_rule.FAIL_INSUFFICIENT_SUPPORT: The estimated moderation points in the predicted direction but does not pass the frozen support gate.
claim_rule.NOT_ESTIMABLE: The archived split sample does not satisfy the frozen estimability gate; no retuning is permitted.

prohibited_post_readout_actions: add species traits to rescue support
switch from phase-centered holdout mismatch to raw mismatch as the primary response
promote a descriptive secondary result to the primary test

implementation_clarification_before_read.calibration_observation_definition: rows with finite arr_GAM_mean and gr_mn used by the timing-gain regression
implementation_clarification_before_read.cell_greenup_baseline_weighting: mean across unique cell x year gr_mn values in calibration years, so species replication does not reweight years
